record.original_question: If G is a triangulation of a surface of genus g and 1 ≤ h < g, must G contain a cycle that separates the surface into two pieces of genera h and g−h?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 6.5 Let G be a triangulation of a surface of genus g, and let 1 ≤ h < g. Then G contains a cycle that separates the surface into two surfaces of genus h and g − h.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a graph embedded as a triangulation of a closed orientable surface $\Sigma$ of genus $g \geq 2$ (so every face of the embedding is bounded by exactly three edges). A cycle $C$ in $G$ is called surface-separating if $\Sigma \setminus C$ has two connected components; in that case, capping off each component along $C$ produces two closed orientable surfaces whose genera $g_1, g_2$ satisfy $g_1 + g_2 = g$, and we say $C$ has type $\{g_1, g_2\}$.

Question: For every integer $h$ with $1 \leq h < g$, must $G$ contain a surface-separating cycle of type $\{h, g-h\}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (that triangulations of genus g contain a separating cycle of every type h, 1≤h<g) is largely open, but a stronger uniform version has counterexamples. Jungerman/Ringel-type complete-graph triangulations have been used to confirm existence of some splitting cycles, and "Some Triangulated Surfaces without Balanced Splitting" (Graphs and Combinatorics, 2016) provides triangulations lacking splitting cycles of certain types, refuting the strongest forms of the conjecture for particular (g,h). The general conjecture as stated remains listed as open in Mohar–Thomassen's problem list.

status_evidence.title: Problems from the book Graphs on Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 5.9.5: every triangulation of an orientable surface of genus g contains a surface-separating cycle into pieces of genera h and g-h.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed as open in Mohar–Thomassen's problem collection.

status_evidence.title: Some Triangulated Surfaces without Balanced Splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples to a stronger conjecture claiming G should contain splitting cycles of every possible type.
status_evidence.claim: Counterexamples are known to the full strength of the conjecture for some specific g,h.

status_evidence.title: On a Conjecture of Thomassen
status_evidence.snippet: Develops tools toward Thomassen's separating cycle conjecture in triangulations.
status_evidence.claim: Active research toward, but not full resolution of, the conjecture.
